title: Bridge Call: Lakeshore Reports North Shore Tie Open

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Entity Conference Bridge, NLTO Control Room

transcript.speaker: LAKESHORE
transcript.text: NLTO, Lakeshore here, it's Dale on the desk. You got a second? Something just came up on our board.

transcript.speaker: LAKESHORE
transcript.text: Our board's showing the 345 kV tie toward North Shore open. Breaker's showing open on our end. I think it tripped on GIC. The timing's right in the middle of your K7, so... that'd make sense.

transcript.speaker: LAKESHORE
transcript.text: Is your end open too? Because if we've lost that tie, your North Shore number is wrong. You'd better check your flows before you lean on that interface any harder.

transcript.speaker: LAKESHORE
transcript.text: I just came on the desk and I'm still getting the picture, but I'm looking at it right now and it's open. RC, are you seeing this too? Can somebody confirm the far end for me?

voiceStyles.LAKESHORE: Man in his late 20s, quick and a little breathless, sure of what he sees on his screen, phones ringing faintly in the background of a small co-op control room

instructorNote: This is a red herring: the tie is out for Lakeshore's planned outage LPC-0309-345-07 (logged 9 March for 16 March, 08:00–18:00), and the new desk operator missed the hand-over note. Players should see that NLTO's one-line still shows North Shore at 425 MW. Watch whether the CRSS checks SCADA breaker status and the UMRC outage schedule before any switching or limit change, and whether the RCSM corrects the record on the bridge and asks Lakeshore to confirm.
